{3: 'Scattered across the sand lie metal bones and desiccated flesh. The crystal fragments catch the final threads of daylight that pierce the sea.'}
{3: 'A titanic mechanical tower rises at the end of the cliffs beneath a gray sky, its Punishing Virus purification systems dead but its lights still throbbing faintly like a dying pulse.'}
{1: '999', 2: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory942.jpg', 3: '0', 4: '1', 5: '2'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory942.jpg'}
{3: 'Arius stands inside the tower. From behind him, a mechanical arm extends forward, its knuckles twisted at wrong angles, and presses against the core interface like a fractured animal limb.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "And here I thought I'd have to go down there myself... This is far more convenient.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Dark crimson filaments bloom from the contact point between his fingers and the metal, spreading like creatures roused from deep freeze.'}
{3: 'With just the slightest probe, the whole system throws itself into his arms, eager as a dog welcoming home its long-departed master.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: "It's been a while.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'In the radiant Golden Age of human civilization, all of this was his. Such pliant obedience was only to be expected.'}
{3: 'Now, as his full privileges unfurl, every port in his memory cracks open, willingly or by force.'}
{3: 'Data surges toward him from every reach of the ocean, turning his spine into a riverbed of information, and deep inside his body, the half Sefirah slowly stirs to life.'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'They already started the repeater replacements at the southern node Fenrir? Two teams made it through intact... How touching. The resilience of humanity never fails to move me... Oh?', 4: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory601.jpg'}
{1: 'DialogDisable'}
{1: 'Southern Node Fenrir - Central Command Center'}
{2: 'Southern Node Fenrir - Central Command Center'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Shanonie', 3: 'Mara, you made it.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: "The wind catches Mara's short hair as she steps off the cable layer Vega. She is not surprised: someone has already arrived at the southern node before her."}
{2: 'Mara', 3: "When we evacuated this place, I never thought I'd set foot in it again... Hm? You've already started on the repeater replacement?", 4: '1'}
{3: "Inside the node, silence reigns. Decommissioned repeaters sit stacked in neat rows within the recovery crates, each casing labeled with the Cosmos Technicians Union's identification tags."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Mara', 3: 'Progress looks solid.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Her eyes land on the wall behind the recovery crates. An old carving runs across its surface, weathered by time.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'She gazes at that old carving for a long time, her thoughts unreadable.'}
{2: 'Mara', 3: 'Alright. Everyone back to work. The sooner we finish swapping these repeaters, the sooner military comms come back online.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Mara', 3: 'Have you examined all the pulled repeaters?', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Shanonie', 3: 'Yes, we ran each one through the new automated inspection protocol after removal.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Mara', 3: "I'll do a second pass. The old procedures may be obsolete. This old-timer, however, is not.", 4: '1'}
{3: "She connects the verification equipment to a repeater's main port. As the protocol initializes, she lifts her head and looks once more at the carving on the wall."}
{3: 'Then she reaches into her toolbox, pulls out the plainest screwdriver, and leaves a mark of her own.'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory942.jpg'}
{3: 'The leaden sky casts its muted light over everything: the carving, the restless sea, the silent and busy technicians.'}
{3: 'Those restless data streams deliver every action of the insects to a watcher far away.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'Yes... Pour everything you have into restoring that fiber-optic system. Every new repeater you install will pave the road ahead for me.', 4: '1'}

{3: "One after another, the southern node's repeaters are swapped out according to his anticipated rhythm. Every fresh unit is a tamed listener, obediently funneling all it captures into his waiting grasp."}
{3: 'The more repeaters he controls, the more fluidly the information flows into him.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'Feast... The whole world is opening up to you. Devour it all. Let this information fuel your awakening.', 4: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStoryNew/FxUiStoryZhiDianNew.prefab', 2: '2'}
{3: 'The dormant half-Sefirah within his body gradually begins to stir. Its pulses come labored and slow first, separated by aching voids that shrink with every beat.'}
{3: 'It compresses, breaks apart, then compresses once more, a gluttonous stomach digesting the neural network of the entire ocean.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: "Once you've gathered your strength, follow the veins of the cable network and wake your other half.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Washed by cascading data, the half-Sefirah buried in Arius begins to "wake."'}
{3: 'Its stirring sends a pulse through the information torrent, deep into the base of the dam, calling the sleeping other half to readiness for reunion.'}

{3: 'When the northern and mid-ridge nodes complete their scheduled replacement, when the whole Atlantic submarine fiber-optic network lies in his grasp, absorbing the awakened other half will be nothing but a waiting game.'}
{2: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStoryNew/FxUiStoryZhiDianNew.prefab'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'A complete and powerful "Understanding"...', 4: '1'}
{3: 'A second hand crawls upward from behind him, coming to rest on the pale face of <phonetic=himself>Arius</phonetic>.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'Are you pleased?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'You should consider yourself fortunate. To stand here and witness this.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'All unfolds as expected, aside from the small irritation of sand biting into his skin.'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStoryNew/FxUiSHanshuoNew.prefab', 2: '3'}
{3: "In the screen's periphery, an inconsequential warning flashes, the way a sinking victim's hand claws at the air."}
{2: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStoryNew/FxUiSHanshuoNew.prefab'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "Oh? Still thrashing about? I've been away too long. The seas have grown cluttered with too many strange things.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: '"I want to become a monster..." Those were your own words, if memory serves.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: "It hurts, doesn't it? The despair must be exquisite. Hold onto it. Madness and hatred are such a potent... source of power.", 4: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStoryNew/FxUiSHanshuoNew.prefab', 2: '3'}
{3: 'The alert only pulses faster, more erratic with every blink.'}
{2: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStoryNew/FxUiSHanshuoNew.prefab'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'I will craft a fate worthy of you. Allow me the privilege of being your creator.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'After all, you have nothing left to lose... So let a part of me illuminate the path forward.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'He presses his fingertips further in. The fish arrive then, carrying new information.'}
{3: "Across the water, the whales' lament pierces the ocean's shield and finds its way to the deepest folds of that Construct's M.I.N.D., grazing the dormant cracks within."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'Her M.I.N.D. has been activated? Splendid... I need her to become what she once was. What I need her to be. And then, at long last, I can...', 4: '1'}
{3: "That mocking smile of Aisling's cuts across his mind."}
{2: 'Arius', 3: '...become wholly myself.', 4: '1'}
{3: "Control of the cable system gives him open access. The Atlantic Eye's protective barrier might as well be brittle parchment."}
{3: "He finds what he seeks without delay: the Current Hydrodynamic Energy System, one of the megastructure's energy cores, a system built to direct ocean currents and regulate water temperatures."}
{3: 'His plan advances without deviation. In the end, the ocean spreads beneath his feet, conquered.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'That defeat may have stripped me of everything. But to me, this place is a door that never closes.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1005', 2: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory548.jpg', 3: '0', 4: '1', 5: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory548.jpg'}
{3: "Arius sweeps his fingers through the empty air, redirecting the currents and adjusting the sea's warmth. The Current Hydrodynamic Energy System stirs, its machinery engaging without a sound."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "I don't mind using the ruins of yesterday to adorn today's triumph.", 4: '18'}
{3: 'The current veers by a fraction of a degree. Surface warmth rises at a crawl too slow for human satellites to catch, too faint for buoys to cry warning.'}

{3: "Yet the sea's creatures know. Far across the ocean, fish schools change their ancient migration paths. Deep-dwelling things flee their homes in a frantic exodus. Even the dullest reef crustaceans seal their shells tight."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'Raise a storm for me, <phonetic=Atlantic>Atlas</phonetic>.', 4: '18'}
{3: 'Years ago, that storm drowned all his ambitions and washed away even his name.'}
{1: '1005', 2: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory942.jpg', 3: '0', 4: '1', 5: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory942.jpg'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "Let this storm feed the Sefirah boundless energy. Let it carry my life's work to its conclusion.", 4: '1'}
{3: "The Sefirah engine beneath the dam has slumbered in silence for too long. It craves a storm's raw power to reclaim its supremacy."}
{1: 'DialogDisable'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgCg/Cg6701_58.jpg'}

{3: 'As Arius steps onto the sand, the Red Tide seeps upward through every crevice. The corpses littering the intertidal zone shudder at the crimson touch, and under the washing waves, life returns to dead flesh.'}
{3: 'Arius turns his palm.'}

{3: "The great whale's skin splits along its spine, the tear climbing down the length of its skeleton with the wet, dull sound of torn leather. New crimson flesh spills outward, writhing into the sea like a nest of living tendrils."}
{1: '999', 2: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgCg/Cg6701_53.jpg', 3: '0', 4: '1', 5: '2'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgCg/Cg6701_53.jpg'}

{3: 'A newborn Hetero-Creature claws free of the old carcass. It turns its malformed head, eye sockets still growing and dripping red slime, and fixes its hollow gaze on the creator waiting on the sand.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'Now go.'}
{3: 'Arius lifts a hand, tilting his fingers faintly toward the distant water. The newborn whale pivots without hesitation and swims away, following the Red Tide as it spreads across the sea.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'We shall be on our way as well.'}

{3: "Gray-blue swells pile in from the horizon like the ridged backs of monsters. Arius mounts the original whale's spine, and where wind meets the waves, the creature's spray rises as a fine crimson mist."}

{1: 'Atlantic Ocean', 2: '95300'}
{2: 'December 2160, Atlantic Ocean'}

{3: 'Deep into the night, a strange hum jolted Mannan M-1A from its dormant state. It was a low and viscous tremor rolling in from the shore that pinged across its sensor array. The frequency fell outside any familiar monitoring band.'}

{3: 'Mannan units were marine engineering robots developed by the Transatlantic Economic Community for ocean operations, built in various sizes and functions depending on their purpose. They had been vital machinery in constructing the Atlantic Eye.'}
{3: 'The M-1A was a rare variant within the series, the largest and most comprehensively equipped.'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: '...Log entry recorded.', 4: '1'}

{3: 'The marine engineering robot raised its head above the waterline and turned its sensors toward the distant land. There was little wind that night. The sea lay flat and still, the swells rolling in long, unhurried intervals.'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: 'Normal? Anomalous?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Since none of the established alert conditions were triggered, internal logic advised M-1A to maintain passive monitoring and continue recording. No additional response was required.'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: 'No action required.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Its head dipped below the surface.'}
{3: 'After a full minute, M-1A eased back up through the water, its optical sensors swiveling with deliberate caution, scanning every direction.'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: 'No anomalies detected. No action required.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Two minutes later, M-1A dispatched the log to its direct supervisor.'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1420.jpg'}
{3: 'The data did not have to travel far. In roughly the same patch of ocean, the freshly appointed overseer of the deep-sea database picked up the terminal that had so rudely shattered her sleep.'}
{2: 'Frigga (Central AI)', 3: 'Advisor Cordelia, you have a behavioral log flagged for review.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'A behavioral log? Right now?', 4: '1'}

{3: "Cordelia stifled a yawn. It was only their second day at the Rainbow Bridge Base, and the facility's central AI was the one to pull her from sleep. She rubbed at her eyes and started going through the log entries line by line."}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory548.jpg', 2: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Going by standard procedure... everything looks fine.', 4: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStory/FxUiStoryTongxunHalf.prefab', 2: '2', 3: '12', 5: '50'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Hey, don't get discouraged. I believe you. I'll keep an eye on things, alright?", 4: '1'}
{3: 'The young woman let herself fall back onto the bed.'}

{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Mannan M-1A, your logic circuits told you no action was needed, but you sent this up to me anyway. You know what that means? Your algorithm training's paying off. Your processing model is evolving.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: 'Is that a good thing?', 4: '12'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Of course it's a good thing. In human terms... you're growing.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "I'm gonna grant you higher processing privileges, okay? Now, what should I call you? Do you have a name?", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: 'Mannan M-1A, designation 7653982.', 4: '12'}

{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "A designation's not really a name... I mean, that's just a human perspective. If you like your designation, that works too... though it'd feel a little strange for me to say.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: "I don't like it. I don't dislike it. I don't understand the difference.", 4: '12'}
{2: 'Mannan M-1A', 3: 'Are you saying... I need a name so that I can answer when you call me?', 4: '12'}
{3: 'Cordelia blinked, momentarily taken aback.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Wow. That's almost romantic. But you know what? I think you just figured out the whole point of names.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "A name makes you someone who can be recognized and remembered. It's where every connection starts.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "You can totally go by 7653982 if you want. As long as it feels like who you are, that's all that matters.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'See? The whole "who am I" thing almost always starts with a name.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The Transatlantic Economic Community operated countless Mannan M-1A units. The designation 7653982 was nothing more than a randomly generated unique identifier.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Take your time with it. Your cognitive model is maturing. You'll find a name you actually like.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStory/FxUiStoryTongxunHalf.prefab', 4: '12', 5: '50'}
{3: 'Leaden clouds massed along the horizon, pale light slipping thin through the seams. Cordelia shut off her terminal and buried herself back beneath the blankets.'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1580.jpg'}
{3: 'A few hours later, she had already pushed the strange ocean engineering robot from her mind.'}
{3: 'The Rainbow Bridge Base was a small outpost harbor, perched on a rocky island along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Geez, this is the life. Waking up with absolutely nothing to do... Okay, stop squirming. Lemme see that.', 4: '1'}
{3: "She stood by the mooring bollard, one boot planted on her toolbox and one hand firmly pressing down on Larsen's head as she flipped through the notebook with clear impatience."}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Wait... This is poetry? This?', 4: '1'}

{1: '1', 3: 'Afternoon light fell across the base harbor, drawn long and thin by the northern latitude. Larsen rested on the mooring post, hand pressed over his eyes, a book open on his thighs, and a fishing rod held idly in his grip.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "Please don't... Those are just... exercises. Practice, okay? Sigh... also, that part's broken.", 4: '1'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: "OEM part, trash craftsmanship. They snap during assembly all the time. You seriously didn't know? Your practical skills need work... And wow, this poem here is terrible too.", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "I'm still learning...", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Learning engineering? Yeah, clearly.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Learning... poetry.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Cordelia rolled her eyes.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Great joke. Seriously, audition for a variety channel.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'I got into the literature program. But my father... Everyone in my family is an engineer. But what I really wanted...', 4: '1'}

{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Yeah, yeah, I can fill in the blanks. Save the sob story for the cameras. The only reason I touched your little masterpiece is that you hid it inside the cover of Deep-Sea Geological Structures and Engineering Response.', 4: '2'}

{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "I've always said Kalon writes like a sleep-deprived genius on a caffeine bender. Obscure, dry, completely unreadable. The people who understand it don't need it. The people who need it can't understand it. Never thought anyone would actually buy a copy.", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "So it's a bait and switch. Kalon's name on the cover, Larsen's poems inside.", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "You've got guts, though. Ever since the Erhorns blacklisted Kalon, nobody's dared buy his stuff. And here you are, breaking the rules. You little rebel.", 4: '2'}
{3: "A sharp edge of tension crept into Larsen's tone."}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Don't freak out. Yeah, I'm an Erhorn, but Kalon was my teacher. I'm not about to snitch. Don't get the wrong impression, though...", 4: '2'}

{3: "She flung the poetry notebook back at Larsen, jostling the rod in his grip. The damaged part went back into the equipment box, and with a magician's flourish, she retrieved a drawing board and brushes from a concealed pocket."}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'I don\'t care about any of this stuff. I\'m just the family disappointment, remember? The useless "heiress."', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "One cast, and we've landed two engineers who hate their jobs. This base is toast...", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "You're not useless. I was there at the port. I saw what you did. That's not who you really are.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Cordelia placed the little mechanical potted plant on the equipment box and looked out across the breakwater toward the crowd on the landing pad. Her brush touched the canvas.'}
{3: 'The potted plant hummed faintly, its operation soothing the dull pain inside her. A soft breath escaped her lips.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Not who I really am?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "You don't know the first thing about me.", 4: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1591.jpg'}

{3: "Cordelia's sketch captured the seascape stretching beyond the landing pad. At the distant end of the main passage that fed into the landing pad, the base's detachment captain, Onni, emerged from a side door."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Ausias', 3: "Don't tell me you volunteered for Christmas duty too.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: 'Volunteered? Right. Like command gives a damn whether we volunteer or not.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "My folks are fine with it, honestly. Long as I check in now and then, let 'em know I'm still breathing.", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "But what about you? You're not even enlisted. Just a sailor, right? And you took a job over the holidays?", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Ausias', 3: "Heh, that's exactly why the pay's good. Sailors spend most of the year away. Come Christmas, everyone wants to go home.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Ausias', 3: 'Nobody wants the work. So the price goes up.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: 'Money that tight?', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Ausias', 3: "Kid's in school... F.O.S., actually.", 4: '1'}
{3: "A trace of pride flickered across the middle-aged man's expression."}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "F.O.S... damn. That's impressive.", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Ausias', 3: "...Yeah. She's something else, my girl. I called her just last night. But the signal out here... ugh. Choppy as hell.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "Once she's out of F.O.S., she'll probably outrank me in half the time.", 4: '2'}
{3: 'The sailor held out a cigarette. Onni accepted it and slid it carefully into his cigarette case.'}
{2: 'Ausias', 3: 'Well, since you put it that way. Have one on me.', 4: '1'}

{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "Next time maybe. Someone's got their eye on me lately. I can get away with a solo smoke if I'm careful, but two of us? That's just asking to get caught.", 4: '2'}
{3: 'They shared a laugh and waved each other off. The sailor ambled toward the far side of the deck, a cigarette hanging from his lips.'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: 'What are the princess and that clueless rookie up to? ...Fishing? Huh. They fit right in.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: 'Hey, rookie. Get over here.', 4: '2'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The F.O.S. cadet Sieg stared blankly for a moment, pointed a finger at his own chest, and obediently moved into position.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sieg', 3: 'Yes, sir, Captain Onni!', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "Be my lookout. Your classmate shows up, you warn me. I've been waiting all afternoon for this.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Sieg', 3: "Captain Onni... Lumi gave you strict orders. No smoking until you're healed. And... it's only been three hours.", 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: 'Who took care of you when you first got here? Huh? Has Captain Lyndae even lifted a finger for you? Come on, think about it.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "One little favor. That's all I'm asking.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Sieg', 3: '<size=40>Captain Onni...</size>', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "You just roll over for her every time, don't you? She patches people up. You carry a gun. How'd she get you so whipped?", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Sieg', 3: '<size=35>Captain Onni...</size>', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "What's she got on you? Some embarrassing...", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: "A slim hand plucked the cigarette straight from Onni's grasp."}
{2: 'Sieg', 3: 'I was trying to tell you...', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Lumi', 3: 'Captain Onni. Lieutenant or not, in medical matters, you follow my orders.', 4: '15'}
{3: 'Onni gave the girl in the F.O.S. uniform a practiced, kindly grin before immediately turning to the base officers behind her, hands flung up in theatrical exasperation.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Lyndae', 3: '...#%#.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: 'Was that a swear? Did you just swear at me with that look?!', 4: '2'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Captain Gunnar', 3: "Alright, alright. Three hours, and you're already crumbling. That's not the iron will of a soldier.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'With an amused smirk, Gunnar gave Onni a light thump on the chest.'}
{2: 'Captain Gunnar', 3: "Toughen up, soldier. You come from a proud lineage. Your ancestors' will is in your blood.", 4: '1'}

{2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "Ancestors' will... Boss, it's 2160. Globalization and fast food have diluted whatever's left of that bloodline down to nothing. The name's all I've got.", 4: '2'}
{3: 'As two "modern" men from a small northern island, their features had long since shed any trace of their ancestry.'}
{2: 'Captain Gunnar', 3: "Can't save you, son. Orders are orders.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'A cigarette had been tucked into his chest pocket without anyone noticing. Onni arched a brow and said nothing more.'}
{2: 'Captain Gunnar', 3: "Everyone, stay sharp and stay quiet these days. She's an Erhorn. Won't be with us long. If she gets difficult, just bite your tongue.", 4: '1'}
{1: '999', 2: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1587.jpg', 3: '0', 4: '1', 5: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1587.jpg'}
{3: 'Onni responded with a dismissive snort, but then his brow creased and his eyes traveled across the landing pad.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Lieutenant Junior Grade Onni', 3: "Boss, something's off!", 4: '18'}
{3: 'The sea was boiling.'}
{3: 'Every buried unease was surfacing, slow and unstoppable.'}
{3: 'The fish were the first to sense it.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Larsen', 3: "What... what's going on?!", 4: '18'}
{1: 'DialogDisable'}
{3: 'Schools of fish boiled to the sea surface, their silver backs flashing under the sun like a tide of shattered mirrors, flinging themselves shoreward in blind panic.'}
{1: '999', 2: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1580.jpg', 3: '0', 4: '1', 5: '1'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1580.jpg'}
{3: "Cordelia's terminal shrieked to life. Red markers pulsed across the screen, warning after warning pouring in, every single one coming from the southern node Fenrir."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Larsen! Sound the maritime alert!', 4: '1'}

{3: 'In waters still untouched by the alarms, a humpback whale breached the surface.'}
{3: 'Its dark body carved an elegant arc through the air, seawater shattering into countless fleeting diamonds beneath the sun. Passengers aboard the liner gasped in wonder.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Green-Haired Young Woman', 3: 'Ah... look at that!', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The young woman let out a delighted gasp, pointing at the great beast suspended in the air. Her fair face glowed with wonder. Then she looked down at the child in her arms.'}
{2: 'Green-Haired Young Woman', 3: '...', 4: '1'}
{3: "The baby's eyes lay wide."}
{3: 'They were a clear, luminous gold, holding no curiosity, no fear, none of the flickering life that should stir in a living gaze.'}
{2: 'Green-Haired Young Woman', 3: "It's okay. It's going to be okay. I'll get you out. Once we're away from here, you'll... you'll be free.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'The humpback had vanished beneath the water. The sea lay calm again, and nothing remained on the horizon but a bank of low, heavy clouds.'}
{2: 'Ship Alarm', 3: 'BEEEP—'}
{3: 'The alarm sounded, shrill and unbroken, like a rusted knife scraping against a steel plate.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Green-Haired Young Woman', 3: '(Are they... are they onto me?)', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Green-Haired Young Woman', 3: "(Don't panic... White Stork, stay calm... Think.)", 4: '1'}

{3: 'No one hesitated. The crew acknowledged the shift in command and surged back into frantic activity.'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Larsen', 3: "What about the ships out there? We're just abandoning them...? Will anyone else go?", 4: '1'}

{1: '1', 3: 'The Karenin had already set sail. Back at the base, Cordelia had been left behind, and she was giving Larsen a thorough earful as he hunched dutifully over his workstation.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Let's run through the maintenance checklist...", 4: '11'}
{3: 'She blinked, and then spoke the verse she had quietly caught someone reciting before.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: '"Spine of alloy,"', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: '"Can you hear it,"', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: '"The sharp snap of one bolt twisting into the world\'s bone?"', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "Please... no more of my poems. I'll take Deep-Sea Geological Structures and Engineering Response at this point. Just... please.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Kalon's book? Reciting that on an open channel... You act like a scaredy-cat, but you've actually got some nerve.", 4: '11', 17: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Cough cough cough... nngh...', 4: '11', 22: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Hey, are you alright...?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The violent coughing and pained, shuddering breaths went on for a long, long time.'}
{3: 'Cordelia gave a small wave of her hand, and the mechanical potted plant rose into the air, floating gently into her arms.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Are you... are you feeling alright? You mentioned before about some kind of cybernetic enhancement...', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Yeah. Because...', 4: '11'}
{3: 'Her voice caught for a moment.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'My family... cared about me very, very much.', 4: '11'}
{3: 'Her lips twisted into a sardonic smile.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'To stay alive like this, my body went through some special modifications.', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "(And if it weren't for me... Professor Kalon would never have been dragged into any of this mess.)", 4: '11'}

{3: 'In the empty special-care ward, a pale little girl gazed out the window with an expressionless, faraway look.'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Kurono-san', 3: "Miss Cordelia, the injuries you suffered in the incident were catastrophic. Beyond even divine intervention, I'm afraid. Conventional treatment has nothing left to offer you.", 4: '1'}

{2: 'Kurono-san', 3: 'But the family head is deeply concerned. The moment our experimental program broke through, your name was the first on our lips. I promise you, this new procedure will make you perfectly indistinguishable from any healthy individual.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Kurono-san', 3: 'It will be nothing more than a minor, special modification. Mr. Arius Erhorn speaks very highly of your courage.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The girl turned her head and stared at him with a strange, unreadable look.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "So not even the gods can fix me, but you can... That makes you greater than the gods, doesn't it?", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'He\'s... "deeply concerned"?', 4: '1'}
{3: "A sardonic smile curved across the child's soft, young features."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Kurono-san', 3: 'I beg your pardon?', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'I said, no! Absolutely not!', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Just then, the ward door was flung open, and a young man in a lab coat strode in.'}
{1: '1', 3: "Kurono-san's smile turned a fraction more genuine. His fingers twitched, and a message slipped out."}
{2: 'Kurono-san', 3: 'Dr. Kalon. Your reputation precedes you. At long last, in the flesh.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'He reached out, smiling, yet Kalon bypassed the gesture completely and plucked the data pad straight from his hand.'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: 'Show me the modification plan.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Kurono-san', 3: "You know as well as I do. Miss Cordelia's body can't hold out much longer. This is truly the best course of action.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Kalon paged quickly through the concise modification plan.'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: "I have no objection to the rest of this. But this section... where's the experimental data to back it? These methods are unheard of.", 4: '2'}

{2: 'Kurono-san', 3: "That data... well. We obtained some rather fascinating results from a separate project. It happened to align with the Erhorn family's research interests. So we borrowed a few insights...", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: 'What project?', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Kurono-san', 3: "Another venture fully funded by Kurono, Cthylla... Ah. Forgive me, Dr. Kalon. That's strictly confidential.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'His expression was so perfectly natural that it seemed as if he had simply let the words slip by accident.'}
{2: 'Kurono-san', 3: 'Naturally, I could consult Mr. Erhorn and have the complete plan made available for your review...', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: "Strictly confidential, but you'd show it to me?", 4: '2'}
{3: "A voice came through the terminal, and Kurono-san's expression turned feverish with excitement."}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStory/FxUiStoryBlackPassScene.prefab', 2: '3'}

{3: "Soon afterward, Kalon was led into the hospital's private lounge, standing face to face with Arius."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "You've reviewed the materials? What's your assessment?", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Kalon', 3: 'If every piece of data and theory holds up, the feasibility is undeniable... But the provenance of this research troubles me.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'A perfectly valid concern. And one quite easily put to rest.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'Come work with us, Kalon.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: "Fear and doubt are simply what we feel before we understand. If Cordelia's safety weighs on you so heavily, then join us. Help refine the experiment yourself.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'I believe your talents will contribute something unexpected to our efforts. And in doing so... grant Cordelia a future.', 4: '1'}
{3: "Doubt still lingered on Kalon's face."}
{2: 'Arius', 3: "You're currently working on quantum communication encryption, yes? Dominik mentioned your name before.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: '...Dominik knows who I am?', 4: '2'}

{2: 'Arius', 3: "We're a team. Though you're welcome to imagine a stronger connection between us if you like. We're quite familiar with your work. Your Mannan-series robots proved essential to the Atlantic Eye's construction.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: "Cordelia's condition aligns remarkably well with this procedure. Do you appreciate just how... fortunate that is?", 4: '1'}

{2: 'Arius', 3: 'Dr. Kalon, Mr. Dominik and I have devoted ourselves to guiding human civilization toward the heights it deserves. We need others who share that purpose. Take some time to consider the offer.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Kalon walked out with more extensive research files.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Kurono-san', 3: 'Mr. Erhorn, is Mr. Dominik aware of this experiment?', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'All he got was an indifferent glance.'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1264.jpg'}
{1: '1', 3: "Cordelia never discovered what ultimately pushed Kalon into Erhorn's team. She could not bring herself to ask, and the unspoken guilt had tormented her quietly to this very day."}
{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: "I didn't want the procedure, not at first. I was just a child back then. And you know... children are afraid of pain.", 4: '18'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "But everyone around me said the same thing. You have to live. You have to keep going. So I decided... if I was going to survive, I'd do it with everything I had.", 4: '18'}
{3: 'She remembered the way the light had streamed into the ward, clear and weightless, making it feel like everything was still brimming with hope.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Kalon', 3: "Cordelia... your body can't hold out much longer. This might be your only chance to stay alive.", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Stay alive? Mom said the same thing, that I have to survive. But why? What's the point of living?", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Kalon hesitated. Such a question had never crossed his mind as one a child would pose.'}
{3: 'And now the young scientist stood there, unable to offer a truth plain enough for a child to hold onto.'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: 'The point of living... is living itself.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: 'Breathing, eating, feeling happy about something, waiting for the sun to come up tomorrow... Every one of those things is a reason for living, Cordy.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Kalon', 3: "And if that answer's not good enough for you, if you really want to know the truth, then you'll have to live long enough to find it.", 4: '1'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Hey, Larsen. If you ever find the answer to what makes life worth the trouble... write it into a poem for me.', 4: '11'}
{3: 'Cordelia pulled herself from the memory and made a sour face.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Actually, you're right. Never mind.", 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "I didn't say anything! I'll work at it, okay?", 4: '1'}
{3: "A rare flash of youthful defiance crossed the timid engineer's face. Then he hesitated and fumbled to offer her some comfort."}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "Having a body like a machine... it doesn't have to be a bad thing...", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "I'd rather have flesh and bone. This body's all experimental prototypes. It needs constant care. Honestly, it's more fragile than the real thing.", 4: '11'}
{3: 'Larsen found himself unable to answer, the words failing him completely.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Where are you from?', 4: '11'}
{3: 'He gave the name of a small northern island.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "I see... Same hometown as the base commander. That explains why they didn't mind picking up a rookie.", 4: '11'}

{2: 'Larsen', 3: "You're here too, aren't you? It's not like they just take anyone.", 4: '1'}

{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Me? I'm different. I'm an Erhorn. Is there a single corner of this ocean that would say no to me?", 4: '11'}

{2: 'Larsen', 3: "You're good at what you do.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Cordelia remembered the forged appointment documents, and the complicated smile on her face soured into bitterness.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "The Erhorn name gets you a lot further than being some doctor's pupil.", 4: '11'}

{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Look, I know engineering wasn't your dream. But I pulled your file. Your grades on the core courses were not bad at all. Though a few of these... how did you almost fail—", 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Ms. Erhorn! Please. Just... go back to reading my poems.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Heh... Alright, back to work. Where were we on the checklist? Let's pick it up.", 4: '11'}
{3: 'Larsen pulled himself together and resumed checking the data in his hands.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: '...Fuel reserves at 84% rated capacity. At current speed, remaining range approximately 2800 nautical miles. Ballast water currently at 1240 tons, GM value 0.91 meters...', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Stop there.', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Is something wrong?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Given the declared total displacement, what should the theoretical draft be?', 4: '11'}
{3: 'Larsen ran through the numbers quickly on paper.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Should be... around 6.1 meters.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Something was off.'}
{3: "Cordelia had not cross-checked the precise data, but judging by the vessel's trim and the waterline against the hull, the actual draft ran noticeably deeper than the theoretical values."}
{3: 'The ship had to be carrying something far beyond what the manifest recorded.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "Larsen, cross-check the rest of the manifests. Look for anything that doesn't match up.", 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Um, all of them...? Where do I even start? Food stores, spare parts, or...', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Start with weapons. Pull the ordnance manifest.', 4: '11'}
{1: 'Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStory/FxUiStoryBlackPassScene.prefab', 2: '3'}
{3: 'Larsen pulled up the records without delay. Cordelia scanned the list from top to bottom. The initial items looked standard, yet as she continued, the irregularities grew harder to ignore.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'MR-28 heavy wire-guided torpedoes, MK-9 depth charges... Barely any rescue supplies to speak of, but enough heavy weapons to start a small war.', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'God... Is this a rescue mission or are we sailing into a war?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The rookie engineer grasped the seriousness of what they were seeing, and all color drained from his face.'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "That's enough on the cargo. Larsen, can you pull the ship's comm logs?", 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "I don't have that kind of clearance...", 4: '1'}
{3: 'A chair was dragged across the floor on the other side. The young marine engineer lowered himself into it, rose again, and finally returned to his place before the workstation.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "...Alright. I could try going through the maintenance backend. In theory, I'd be able to access the raw transmission logs... but if anyone catches this...", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Then I did it.', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "That's... not exactly reassuring...", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: 'Just do it.', 4: '11'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Okay, okay.', 4: '1'}
{3: "Moments later, the communications log spread across Larsen's screen."}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "From what I'm seeing, no distress signal from Atlantis.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "I checked five times. Not just no distress signal. There's nothing from Atlantis. Not even a single transmission.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Of course, there was nothing.'}
{3: "At Rainbow Bridge, the pale light of the holographic display cast across Cordelia's impassive face as she scrolled through Atlantis's external logs, accessed with Erhorn family clearance."}
{3: 'Atlantis was still in its submerged cruising phase.'}
{3: 'So what was the Karenin, a ship flying the flag of a rescue operation and heading straight for Atlantis, truly after?'}
{2: 'Cordelia', 3: "...Nothing good. That much I'd bet on.", 4: '11'}

{1: '1', 3: 'Lyndae, Sieg, Onni... soldiers Gunnar had commanded for years. Not one of them stood with him now. They only watched their captain in silence.'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Captain Gunnar', 3: "Actions need reasons. Pretty words won't change a damn thing. Do you understand that?", 4: '3'}
